name: Juicy wash and go
tagline: Conditioned, clumped and fully dried, so the definition is still there on day three.
image_alt: A rounded wash-and-go with defined coils and the front curls left to fall forward.
description: A botanical-forward wash and go: are you ready, the ten-step routine with what to use at each step, and how to set it fully dry and keep it for a week.
intro: A juicy wash and go is not a wet one. It is conditioned, well clumped, dried all the way through, then released gently. This plan leans on botanical gels, protects your hair from the heat you set it with, and skips air-drying.

causes.title: What juicy actually means
causes.intro: Four words get used as if they mean the same thing. They overlap, but they are not identical.
items: Hydrated
Hair that is well conditioned and flexible.
This is the foundation. No gel can make up for tangled, under-conditioned hair.
Juicy-looking
The look of defined, well-conditioned coils that catch the light.
It comes from clumping and conditioning, not from being wet.
A wet-looking wash and go
A styling finish, while the hair is still wet.
It looks great for twenty minutes. It is not the goal.
A properly set wash and go
A style that has dried completely, formed its shape and held it.
This is the goal. The set is the part people rush.
What a botanical gel does
Plant gels such as flax, okra, aloe and marshmallow give slip while you style, help strands group into clumps, and leave a dried film that keeps the shape. That film is a scaffold for the style.
It does not seal water inside the strand, and it does not stop breakage. The honest promise is a more manageable style with less daily handling.

routine.title: The routine
routine.intro: One wash, style and set from start to finish. Each step shows what to reach for, and you only need one product per step. Give yourself a free afternoon the first time.

wash.title: Wash, style and set
steps: Saturate
Wet your hair in four to eight sections and make sure the roots and the middle of each section are soaked. Dense hair can be dripping outside and still dry in the center.
Shampoo
Shampoo the scalp, let the lather rinse down the lengths, and rinse well. No need to scrub the ends. Clarify or chelate only when your hair asks for it.
Deep condition
Apply a moisture-rich mask to each section and leave it on for as long as the label says. Warmth is fine if the label allows it.
Detangle
Fingers first, then a wide-tooth comb or detangling brush, working from the ends up, with enough conditioner for real slip. Get the shed hair out now, before any gel goes on.
Rinse and check
Hair should feel soft, slippery and flexible, not waxy.
Leave-in, with heat protection
Because we set with heat, your leave-in should protect from it. Pick one with heat protection built in, or add protection in step 8. Use it on soaking wet hair, just enough for slip.

steps.label: Leave-ins with heat protection
steps.note: Test a new leave-in and gel pairing on one small section first. If they flake or turn white together, they are not friends.

steps: Gel and shape

Your hair should still be very wet, not damp. Work in small sections with praying hands and smooth from roots to ends, with gentle tension to elongate. Shingle only the sections that need more definition, then leave each one alone.

steps.label: Gels, softest hold to firmest
steps.note: Start with one gel. Add a second only if you need more hold. Read the whole ingredient list: water first, then plant extracts, pectin or gums is what botanical-forward looks like.

steps: Add heat protection
If your leave-in does not already protect from heat, mist or smooth on a heat protectant before you dry. Skip this step if it does.
Set it, fully dry

Arrange the coils in their final shape, then dry them completely, roots and middle included. A hooded dryer is best. No hooded dryer? Use a diffuser, or a blow dryer on low heat and low airflow. Let the hair cool before you touch it, and check the roots and nape with your fingertips: cool and damp means keep going.
Release and polish

When it is fully dry and cool, rub a drop or two of lightweight oil between your palms, scrunch the lengths gently, and break the cast without pulling every clump apart. You are going for soft definition, not an oil slick.

between.title: The first week
groups: Break the cast once it is fully dry. Arrange the roots. Protect it at night.
Wear it loose or in a loose pineapple. Satin bonnet at night. Do not add gel just because the hair has moved.
Mist lightly, put a tiny amount of leave-in on frizzy spots, smooth those sections, add a little compatible gel only where needed, and dry them completely.
Keep the ends protected at night and avoid tight styles. Wash sooner if your scalp needs it or the style gets coated or tangled.

techniques.title: The rules of this plan
techniques.intro: A few choices make this a juicy wash and go and not just a wash and go.
items: Dry it completely, no air-drying
A complete set is the whole point. Dry the hair fully under a hooded dryer, diffuser or blow dryer. Do not shortcut it by air-drying or by sleeping on damp hair.

Drying time depends on density, length, how much product you used and your dryer, so go by how the hair feels, not by a number of minutes. With a diffuser or blow dryer, use low airflow and moderate heat, and do not keep moving the coils around.
Plant-forward gels
Build your hold from gels made with plant ingredients like flax, aloe, marshmallow and pectin. Some of the firmer holds also use a synthetic thickener or polymer, and we point those out.
A plant extract on the label does not mean a formula is free of synthetic polymers. Read the whole ingredient list.
Clump, then do not touch
Build coherent groups of coils and leave them alone.
Every extra rake, separation or fluff before the set is dry breaks definition you have just made.
Do not break the cast early
The cast is the dried gel film. A firm cast is not a problem. It is what makes the style last.
Judge softness after it is dry and released, not while the gel is still setting.
Use less product than you think
One gel to start. A second only if you need more hold.
It is much easier to find what works, and avoid buildup, when only one thing changes at a time.
Protect the result
Satin bonnet or pillowcase, ends tucked in, nothing tight.
Your night routine decides how much of the definition survives.

ing.title: What to look for on a label
ing.intro: The plant ingredients that do the styling work. Hover any name to see what it is.
items: Flaxseed and okra
Mucilage that gives slip while you style and forms a film as it dries. Flexible to firm, depending on the formula.
cosmetic
Film formers
properties/film-former/
Marshmallow root and slippery elm
Slippery plant extracts for glide while you detangle and apply.
cosmetic
Slip
properties/slip-detangler/
Aloe and agave
Water-loving ingredients that add a light, flexible base.
cosmetic
Humectants
properties/humectant/
Pectin, xanthan and guar
Plant gums that thicken the gel and form the film that holds the clump.
cosmetic
Film formers
properties/film-former/
Oils and fatty alcohols
Jojoba, squalane, cetearyl alcohol. Softness and less friction. Keep oil for the finish.
established

trouble.title: If something feels off
items: Crunchy and stiff
A strong cast or too much gel. Wait until it is completely dry before scrunching, and use less next time.
Flakes or white residue
Two products that do not layer well, or too many layers. Simplify and test pairs on one section.
Dry-looking curls
Not enough conditioning, or buildup. Look at your deep conditioner and your cleansing before adding product.
Wet-looking but sticky
It has not finished drying, or the formula is very humectant-heavy. Keep drying, then adjust.
Frizz right away
Poor clumping or too little hold. Smaller sections, even distribution, hands off.
Frizz after day two
Friction, humidity or weak hold. Improve the set and your night protection.
Frizz at the nape
Detangle the nape well before styling and protect it overnight.
Flat roots
Too much product near the scalp. Use less at the roots.

end.title: After your first set
notes: Judge your wash and go once it is dry and released, not while it is wet. That is the only version that tells you whether it worked.

A homemade gel is a different thing: water-based recipes grow bacteria unless they are properly preserved, and refrigerating or adding vitamin E does not fix that. If you make your own, make a tiny batch, use clean tools, keep it cold and throw it out quickly.

Gel was spread evenly, roots to ends
Roots and inside were completely dry

ready.title: Are you ready to style?
ready.intro: You don't need perfect hair first. You need hair that is manageable. Tap through these five, and we'll tell you where to start.
items: It detangles without a fight
With conditioner in, your hair comes apart without a struggle.
Your ends feel okay
Not rough, not knotted. Check the last few inches first.
Nothing feels coated
No film, no waxy feel, no heavy leftovers from old product.
It's not brittle
It bends before it breaks.
Your scalp feels good
Clean and comfortable, with no itch or tightness you're trying to ignore.

verdict.wait: {n} of {total} answered. Do the rest and we'll tell you where to start.

verdict.four: So close. You can start the routine now, or open the optional prep below for a gentler runway.
verdict.few: Let's get your hair ready first. We opened the optional prep for you: a few easy weeks, then the routine.

prep.title: Optional prep
prep.intro: If your hair is dry, tangled, breaking or coated, give it a little time before the full routine. Skip this if you answered yes to everything.
items: Reset
Shampoo, clarify if there is buildup, chelate if your water is hard, deep condition, detangle, add a light leave-in, and put it in a loose protective style.
Ceramide and lipid conditioning
A conditioner with ceramides and other supportive lipids. Then your normal leave-in and a protective style.
Strength check
Only if your hair has been bleached, relaxed, heavily heat-styled or is breaking. Otherwise deep condition as normal.
Softness check
Moisture deep conditioner, gentle detangling, leave-in, low-manipulation style. Aim for flexible and manageable, not as soft as possible.
prep.note: If your hair is badly damaged or chemically processed, a stylist may be the best first step.
